title: Oppo releases ColorOS 16 August update with new features and improvements
description: Oppo has just started seeding an update to the existing ColorOS 16 to eligible devices. The August update brings an AI Remix Collage, security improvements, new Home Screen functionalities, Currency Converter widgets and new Notes features. The AI Remix Collage now has a Smart Cutout that allows you to create stickers or advanced collages with layer controls. The Security and Phone Manager apps can block suspicious app activity on the fly, as well as malicious popups and rogue apps that drain your battery. Users will receive real-time alerts when something is happening. With the new...

title: The Samsung Galaxy S26 FE arrives with a new chipset and a host of One UI 9 features
description: The Samsung Galaxy S26 FE may as well have been called the S26 AI. When designing this phone, the company’s focus was on new AI features and the utility they offer in day-to-day tasks. There are hardware upgrades too, though pluralizing that word may be a stretch. The funny thing is that when Samsung unveiled the S26 FE, it didn’t mention the chipset – we're quite certain that it is the Exynos 2500. This 3nm chip was only featured on the Galaxy Z Flip7 until now and it is the biggest upgrade over the Galaxy S25 FE, which used the Exynos 2400. The 2500 was the first chipset to be fabbed on...

title: Redmi Note 17 and Redmi Note 17 5G focus on big batteries and displays
description: Xiaomi's global Redmi Note 17 family is here and we're looking at the two non-Pro models now (head this way for the Pros). The Redmi Note 17 and Redmi Note 17 5G are nearly identical phones, save for some obvious differences - the choice of chipset and the ability to connect to 5G. The Redmi Note 17 uses the 6nm Snapdragon 6s Gen 2 with either 4GB, 6GB, or 8GB of RAM. Its CPU clocks up to 2.9GHz, and its modem supports up to 4G. The Redmi Note 17 5G uses a newer, 4nm Snapdragon 4 Gen 4 with a 2.3GHz CPU, either 6GB or 8GB of packaged RAM, and, of course, 5G. It's not exactly clear...

title: Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro Max review
Redmi Note 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max bring Si/C batteries and Snapdragon 6 chips
description: The Redmi Note 17 series is going global – these phones are slightly different from the Note 17 models that we saw in China and that will soon be available in India. Here we will focus on the two Pro models, but Xiaomi also unveiled the Redmi Note 17 5G and 4G. Those will be covered in a separate post. Redmi Note 17 Pro and Redmi Note 17 Pro Max The Redmi Note 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max are the successors to the Redmi Note 15 Pro and 15 Pro+ from late last year. Both have 6.83” OLED displays, but this year they pack even bigger batteries with faster charging. Both phones use...

title: Lava Bold N4 Lite debuts with 6.56-inch screen, 5,000mAh battery
description: Lava seems to have skipped the Bold N3 series as the company has just launched the Bold N4 Lite in India. It appears to be the successor to the Bold N2 Lite. The new budget smartphone comes with basic specifications and runs Android 16 Go Edition. The Lava Bold N4 Lite comes with a 6.56-inch LCD display and is powered by the Unisoc 9863A chipset. It gets 3GB of RAM and 32GB of internal storage, which is expandable up to 64GB with a microSD card. It packs a 5,000mAh battery, an 8MP rear camera, and a 5MP front facing unit for selfies and video calls. The phone runs Android 16 Go...

title: vivo X500 Pro series confirmed to feature 2nm MediaTek chipset
description: vivo continues to share new details about its upcoming X500 series, following the recent confirmation of several key camera features on the X500 Pro Max. The company has now detailed the chipset that will power the X500 Pro models. While vivo has not revealed the chipset’s exact model, it has confirmed that the X500 Pro and X500 Pro Max will be powered by a 2nm MediaTek Dimensity chipset. The new Dimensity chipset is built on TSMC’s second-generation 2nm N2P process and features an all-new GPU architecture and an “ultra-high-performance NPU”. The Pro models will also feature a...

description: Samsung's Galaxy Event day has arrived. It will begin at 12 PM UTC, and you can follow it with us by tuning in to the YouTube stream below. Samsung hasn't revealed what this Galaxy Event will cover, but it doesn't take a genius to figure out it's going to be about the Galaxy S26 FE. title: Realme C100i 4G goes official in India with a 6,500mAh battery
description: Realme C100i 4G, which was unveiled in select markets back in May, has made its way to India with a redesigned rear panel and a smaller battery. The Realme C100i Indian variant is an affordable 4G phone that comes with a 6.8-inch LCD display that supports a 120Hz refresh rate and a peak brightness of 900 nits. It is powered by an octa-core Unisoc T7250 chipset, which is paired with 4GB of LPDDR4X RAM and up to 128GB of UFS 2.2 storage. A microSD card slot is available for storage expansion. At the back, the Realme C100i features an 8MP camera and an LED flash housed inside a...

title: Samsung reportedly decided against a 7,000 mAh battery for the Galaxy S27 Ultra, here's why
description: Back in July, the battery capacity of the upcoming Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra was leaked and purported to be rated at 5,534 mAh, which would yield a typical capacity of 5,700 mAh. That's a big jump for Samsung, from the Galaxy S26 Ultra's 5,000 mAh cell, but it's still tiny in this day and age compared to what the Chinese competition is doing. Today a new rumor from a tipster on X brings us a "what if" scenario. Apparently, Samsung tested a Galaxy S27 Ultra prototype with a 7,000 mAh battery, but in the end decided to stick with the 5,700 mAh to 6,000 mAh range. Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra...

description: Oppo is expected to unveil its Find X10 series in September. While the company has yet to reveal a launch timeline, it has reportedly confirmed that the upcoming phones will feature Tianma OLED displays. According to a report, Oppo and Tianma unveiled the new Tianma Tiangong Screen 2.0 at an event in China, with the technology reportedly set to debut on the upcoming Find X10 series. Oppo Find X9 Pro The report notes that Tianma has used a new N1 primary-colour spectrum material in the panel, reducing harmful blue light by 3.7% while increasing deep-red light output to 5.5%. description: Honor has already confirmed that the Magic9 series is coming in September. You may have been wondering how many devices will be part of the lineup, and today Digital Chat Station has shared the purported answer on Weibo. According to him, we're getting the Magic9, powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 SoC, just like the Magic8 (blame the RAM and storage chip crisis, presumably). This device will have a 6.36-inch screen with a "1.5K" resolution and a "large battery" that isn't detailed any further. title: Here's how Android, iOS, and Harmony OS rank globally
description: Counterpoint Research (CR) just released its report about the best-selling smartphones in the world in the second quarter of this year (April to June), but it also revealed how mobile operating systems are doing. The following is based on Q2 smartphone shipment data, so the percentages aren't of devices in use, but of handsets shipped during that specific quarter. Globally, Android is king with a 75% share, up from 73% in Q1. iOS follows with 20%, down from 22% in Q1. In third and last place is Huawei's HarmonyOS, which has managed to capture a 5% share, just like it did in Q1. In...

description: Yesterday, Nothing unveiled the Nothing OS 5.0 release, based on Android 17. The company also detailed its rollout for all supported devices. And today, right on time, the first open beta build of Nothing OS 5.0 has become available for the Nothing Phone (3). You can download the open beta from this page (scroll down almost to the end to see the link). Well, technically, you're not downloading the new firmware, but the latest Nothing Beta Hub version 2.0 app. You need to use that to get the software update. title: iPhone 17 continues to lead global smartphone sales in Q2 2026
description: Back in May, the base Apple iPhone 17 was the world’s best-selling smartphone for Q1 2026. Now, a new Counterpoint report shows that the iPhone 17 has retained the top spot in global smartphone sales in Q2 2026. According to the research firm’s latest data, the iPhone 17 accounted for 6% of global smartphone unit sales in Q2 2026. Apple also secured five other spots in the top 10. The iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPhone 17 Pro ranked second and third, respectively, while the iPhone 17e and iPhone 16 also made the top 10. title: Google Pixel 11 Pro XL in for review
description: Today, we got the new Pixel 11 lineup on our doorstep, so it's time to start unboxing them one by one. The new phones made somewhat of a negative initial impression for keeping things mostly unchanged, but there are some novelties. Let's dive in! From left to right: Google Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and the Pixel 11 Pro XL The Google Pixel 11 Pro XL is the biggest in the trio, and it feels it. It's tall and wide, and hefty at 226 grams. title: Lenovo Legion Y700 AI tablet unveiled with Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and dual USB-C ports
description: Lenovo teased a new Y700 tablet that scored 4,585,844 on AnTuTu – this was achieved with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 as we now know since Lenovo just unveiled the tablet. Lenovo Legion Y700 AI The Lenovo Legion Y700 AI – yes, it has AI in the name – is smaller than its predecessor. It has an 8.4” OLED display, a 2,560 x 1,600px panel, with 12-bit colors and Dolby Vision support. The display runs at up to 165Hz and can reach 4,000 nits peak brightness. title: Apple schedules iPhone event for September 9
description: Months of rumors and leaks later, we finally have a date for Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro series and first foldable iPhone announcement. Apple has confirmed that its iPhone-focused event will take place on September 9 at 10am PT. The company will host an in-person event at Apple Park in Cupertino, California and will livestream the keynote. The event poster features the tagline “Surprise and Shine,” along with a glowing Apple logo that appears to have sunlight shining through it. title: Samsung Galaxy S27 CAD-based renders leak
description: Yesterday some new CAD-based renders of the upcoming Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra leaked online, and today it's the vanilla Galaxy S27's turn to get the exact same treatment. Immediately you can see a stark difference between the S27 and the S27 Ultra. The top of the line device has a new camera island design, while the entry-level model won't. In fact, the Galaxy S27 looks remarkably similar to the Galaxy S26, with its oval-shaped camera bump that's in the top left corner of the rear. title: Garmin launches the Fenix 9 and Fenix 9 Pro with up to 57 days of battery life
description: Garmin has just launched the Fenix 9 and Fenix 9 Pro smartwatches, with the latter boasting the first full titanium case and largest AMOLED screen in the Fenix line ever. The Fenix 9 has a fiber-reinforced polymer case with a titanium rear cover, and a screen with twice the brightness of its predecessor, with a sapphire crystal on top. It's dive-rated to 40m and has leak-proof buttons. There's also 50% more RAM than on the Fenix 8, and a more powerful map engine with 30% faster panning.
